column1: # The name of an Arabic letter is a spoken thing: نُون is /nuːn/, and the name
# carries no meaning apart from that sound. So a letter name is written the way
# it is said, not letter by letter — noon, not nun.
# This also keeps letter names out of collision with ordinary English words.
# `nun` and `sin` are English words, and `sin_al_qiraah` is not an identifier
# The rule applies ONLY to the name of a letter. Every other term follows the
# derivation in sections 4 to 8: tajwid, not tajweed; haqiqi, not haqeeqi.
